item.title: From AI to Air-Conditioning: The Power Boom in Asia
item.dc:creator: Morgan Stanley
item.description: Morgan Stanley · Thoughts on the Market — Our Asia Energy analyst Mayank Maheshwari discusses how AI, new factories and cooling systems are boosting electricity demand in Asia and reshaping local power structure. Read more insights from Morgan Stanley. ----- Transcript ----- Welcome to Thoughts on the Market. I’m Mayank Maheshwari, Morgan Stanley’s Asia Energy analyst. Today – why power thematic is moving beyond AI. It’s Thursday, November 12th, at 10am in Singapore. Whenever I have a conversation on power, it is mostly thought of as a story about AI. But the electrification super cycle is much broader than just AI. Consensus is underestimating how much power the world will need by the end of the decade. We think global electricity use could reach nearly 36 trillion units by 2030, 15 percent above current market estimates. Outside China, that could reach 23 trillion units, with Asia’s demand growing 20 percent faster than in the U.S. For years, the focus was on the electricity needed by data centers and semiconductor factories. That need is still rising, but AI-related demand is only about a quarter of incremental power demand. New industrial projects and air conditioning are now adding to the pressure. Not surprisingly,…

The dot-com bubble marked a turning point in market history, fueled by the promise of internet technology and a wave of investor enthusiasm. Optimism, easy access to information and a booming economy set the stage for soaring IPOs and rapid market growth - even when fundamentals were hard to pin down. item.title: Singing 'for' the Rain: Investigating Water Scarcity (ft. Jo Harrison, Environment, Planning and Innovation Director at United Utilities)
item.dc:creator: Société Générale
item.description: Société Générale · 2050 Investors — Is the Earth running out of fresh water? The summer of 2022 saw significant droughts across the world, with serious ripple effects from energy shortages to severe food insecurity. But how can we have a water crisis when water makes up close to three quarters of our planet’s surface? In this episode, Kokou Agbo-Bloua looks at how climate change is disrupting our planet’s water cycle. He explores the vast reserves of our planet against the backdrop of dwindling freshwater resources. From record rainless periods in Europe to the water-intensive nature of various industries, he examines the alarming realities and potential solutions to this growing challenge. Exploring global water consumption patterns, he focuses on industries and food items driving high water footprints. The episode sheds light on the water requirements behind everyday products, prompting a deeper reflection on our consumption habits. Expert guest Jo Harrison from water utilities company United Utilities Group PLC also discusses the impacts of climate change on freshwater supply, offering insights into measures taken by water utilities to mitigate its effects. Her expertise extends to leakage reduction strategies…

item.title: Midterms Could Delay the AI Buildout, Not Derail It

item.description: Morgan Stanley · Thoughts on the Market — Concerns over electricity bills and water use are turning into political action. Our Head of Public Policy Research Ariana Salvatore breaks down what the midterms mean for the data center pipeline, hyperscaler CapEx and investors. Read more insights from Morgan Stanley. ----- Transcript ----- Ariana Salvatore: Welcome to Thoughts on the Market. I'm Ariana Salvatore, Head of Public Policy Research at Morgan Stanley. Today, the U.S. midterm elections and what they could mean for the build-out of AI infrastructure. It's Wednesday, November 11th at 10am in New York. Growing concerns around electricity bills, water consumption, and the economic benefits of data centers have translated into meaningful political opposition. And last week's results reinforce just how salient those issues were in voters' decision-making. But what are the practical implications for the build-out? We think that the midterms were actually more likely to change where data centers get built, when they come online, and what cost is associated with doing so, rather than whether they get built at all. We've been flagging political opposition to data centers as a risk for some time, and the election results…

item.title: Playing for Scale: The Future of Sports Investing
item.dc:creator: Goldman Sachs
item.description: Goldman Sachs · Goldman Sachs Exchanges — Investors are finding opportunities in sports as the media rights market surges and team valuations climb, Nicole Pullen Ross, head of the Sports and Entertainment Solutions within Goldman Sachs Private Wealth Management, explains on the Exchanges podcast. Read the related report here. Key Takeaways: The value of sports media rights is soaring: The global sports media market grew 41% from 2020 through 2025 and has continued climbing to an expected $67 billion in 2026. Private equity and institutional investments are accelerating: Surging media rights are the core driver of growth, lifting sports franchise valuations to historic highs. Infrastructure and real estate are key: Modern venues and surrounding entertainment districts create benefits that go beyond game day and complement technology-driven fan personalization. Women’s and college sports are attracting investors: Women’s teams that control their own arenas command higher valuations, and new player-pay rules are prompting college athletic departments to weigh new types of financing. This episode was recorded on October 27, 2026. The opinions and views expressed herein are as of the date of publication, subject to change…

item.title: What's the Risk? 7 Numbers that Reveal Hidden Exposures in Today's Portfolios
item.dc:creator: Apollo
item.description: Apollo · Apollo Insights & Outlook (web) — How well do investors really understand the risks in their portfolios? The S&P 500 includes hundreds of stocks, yet a handful of AI-linked companies drive its returns. The Bloomberg US Aggregate, the benchmark for the US investment-grade bond market, contains thousands of securities, but it is now largely tied to interest rates, and AI borrowers account for more than half of this year’s net investment-grade issuance. Investors may be taking on risks they never intended, obscured by portfolios that appear diversified on the surface.
